findings.title: Pass query results to the new table visualization
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, every table widget receives empty columns, empty metadata, and an empty data array instead of the query's `result`. Consequently, enabling the feature removes all headers and rows from otherwise populated dashboard tables. Wire the actual fields, metadata, and query results into the new visualization before replacing the existing table.

findings.title: Include the organization in the attribute-key cache key
findings.body: The new React Query key contains only filter options, while the request URL depends on `organization.slug`. Two organizations with the same date range and all-projects selection therefore share a cache entry despite querying different endpoints. Switching organizations can reuse the other organization's custom attribute names, and changing the query callback does not invalidate that entry. Include the organization slug or organization-scoped endpoint URL in the key.

findings.title: Normalize timestamp units before merging errors and recording events
findings.body: Nodestore error timestamps are Unix seconds, whereas rrweb recording event timestamps are Unix milliseconds. Comparing them directly makes virtually every error timestamp smaller than the first recording timestamp, so errors that occurred later in the replay are emitted before its first breadcrumb. This gives Seer incorrectly ordered context for summaries and chapters. Normalize both sources to the same unit; the new tests use second-scale recording timestamps and therefore miss this case.

findings.title: Use a time window containing the replay for the error lookup
findings.body: The AI tab's summary request supplies only the replay ID, but this new metadata query is bounded by `get_filter_params`' default date window. Retained replays older than that window can still have their recording segments fetched by ID, while the metadata query returns no rows. Their summaries therefore silently omit all error context. Derive the lookup window from the replay's timestamps or pass an appropriate replay-specific range from the client.

findings.title: Accept the standard permissions-policy violation report type
findings.body: The choices contain `permissions-policy`, but browsers emit Permissions Policy violation reports with type `permissions-policy-violation`. Unlike the previous type annotation, this new `ChoiceField` enforces the list at runtime, so valid browser reports now receive HTTP 422. A mixed batch containing such a report is also rejected before metrics are recorded for any report. Add the actual standardized report type to the accepted choices.

findings.title: Honor falsy results from custom cell renderers
findings.body: Both default-renderer wrappers use `if (cell)` to decide whether the custom renderer handled a cell. However, the documented fallback signal is `undefined`, and valid React results such as `0`, `null`, `false`, and an empty string are falsy. For example, a custom renderer returning `null` to leave a cell blank instead displays the original field value. Check explicitly for `undefined` in both the header and body wrappers.
